mainTopic: The יסוד of the outer מזבח: גג יסוד, and whether the leftover blood (שירים) and squeezing a bird חטאת's blood are essential
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the words "אל יסוד מזבח העולה". The inner altar has no יסוד, and the extra word "מזבח" teaches that blood goes on the top surface of the יסוד (גג יסוד). רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא each argue that a קל וחומר from שירי חטאת already teaches גג יסוד, so the פסוק instead teaches that the altar of the עולה must have a יסוד. The גמרא asks what separates their two wordings. רב אדא בר אהבה says they argue whether the leftover blood (שירים) is essential. רב פפא says everyone agrees שירים are not essential, and they argue about squeezing out the blood of a bird חטאת. A ברייתא about the bulls of יום הכיפורים and the כהן משיח supports רב פפא: even רבי ישמעאל holds that skipping the יסוד does not disqualify, and the פסוק's wording makes the pouring a שירי מצוה. Finally the גמרא challenges רב פפא from a teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school about squeezing a bird's blood, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The inner altar has no base, so the verse must mean the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes ruling out a reversed rule, where blood sprinkled outside would have its leftovers poured on the inner altar. That cannot work, because the inner altar has no יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that blood sprinkled on the outer altar should have its leftovers poured on the inner altar, just as blood sprinkled inside has its leftovers poured outside. But the inner altar has no base at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a thought from the previous page. It rejects the idea that leftover blood from an outer offering could be poured at the inner altar, because the inner altar has no base to pour it on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have reasoned with a neat symmetry: leftovers of inside blood go outside, so leftovers of outside blood should go inside. The symmetry breaks down because only the outer מזבח has a יסוד. So the פסוק must be pointing to the יסוד of the outer altar, the מזבח העולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Outer, meaning the outer altar (מזבח החיצון)
Inner, meaning the inner golden altar (מזבח הפנימי)
The base, a ledge running along the bottom of the outer altar
The inner altar

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an argument that started on the previous page. Don't look for its beginning here. It only finishes the point that the inner altar has no יסוד.

phrases.english: that what is sprinkled outside goes inside,
phrases.notes: He means: the leftover blood of an outer-altar offering would be poured at the inner altar.

phrases.english: just as what is sprinkled inside goes outside;
but there is no base
for the inner altar itself!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵין לוֹ יְסוֹד לִפְנִימִי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from the previous page about where the leftover blood is poured.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reversed idea that leftovers of outer blood could go to the inner altar.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inner altar has no יסוד, so there is nowhere there to pour leftovers.

steps.title: Another reading: the burnt offering's blood must go where there is a base
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a different meaning for the verse. Perhaps it teaches that the sprinkling of an עולה's blood must be done on a part of the altar that has a יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps that is not what the verse means. Maybe it teaches that the altar of the burnt offering, where its blood is sprinkled, must be at a place with a base.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers another way to read "אל יסוד מזבח העולה". This sets up the גמרא's next question about whether the wording fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the verse was read as being about leftover blood. Here it is read as being about the main sprinkling of the עולה. On this reading, the עולה's blood must be put on a corner of the altar that sits above the יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: "Or perhaps it is only...", a phrase that brings in another possible reading
Burnt offering
Its altar, the place where its blood is sprinkled

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is only
that the altar of the burnt offering,
must be at a place with a base.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִזְבְּחָהּ שֶׁל עוֹלָה יְהֵא לַיְסוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sprinkling of an עולה's blood must be on a part of the altar that has a יסוד.

steps.title: The verse says "altar of the burnt offering," not just "burnt offering"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the verse were about the עולה needing a base, it would say "the base of the burnt offering." Instead it says "the base of the altar of the burnt offering."
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written "at the base of the burnt offering"? It is written "at the base of the altar of the burnt offering"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading using the exact words of the פסוק. The extra word "altar" seems to have no purpose if the verse only means the עולה needs a base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the point were only that the עולה's blood needs a יסוד, the short wording "יסוד העולה" would be enough. The added word "מזבח" must be teaching something more, so the reading seems weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is it written...?", a challenge from the exact wording of a verse
The altar of the burnt offering, the outer altar

phrases.english: Is it written "at the base of the burnt offering"?!
It is written "at the base of the altar of the burnt offering"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the verse teaches the עולה's blood must be sprinkled where there is a יסוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "מזבח" would be extra under that reading, since "יסוד העולה" would have been enough.

steps.title: The extra word teaches: on top of the base, not on its side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word "altar" is needed. Without it, one might think the blood goes on the upright side of the יסוד. With it, we learn the blood goes on the top surface of the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had said "at the base of the burnt offering," I would have said the blood goes on the upright side of the base. Now that it says "at the base of the altar of the burnt offering," it means on the top surface of the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading by showing the word "altar" has a job. It tells us exactly where on the יסוד the blood goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יסוד has two surfaces: its upright side wall and its flat top. Mentioning the "altar" ties the יסוד to the altar itself, which points to its top surface (גג). So the word is not extra, and the reading from step 2 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The upright, standing side wall
Roof, here the flat upper surface of the יסוד
"I would have said", a mistaken first thought
Now, that is, given how it is actually written

steps.whatToRemember: The word "מזבח" in "אל יסוד מזבח העולה" teaches that the blood is placed on the top surface of the יסוד (גג יסוד), not on its upright side.

phrases.english: If it were written "at the base of the burnt offering,"
I would have said: on the upright side of the base;
now that it is written "at the base of the altar of the burnt offering,"
it means on the top surface of the base.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word its own teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without "מזבח", one would think the blood goes on the upright side of the יסוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word "מזבח" teaches that the blood goes on the top surface of the יסוד.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: why need a verse? A קל וחומר teaches it
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks why a פסוק is needed to teach גג יסוד. The leftover blood of a חטאת does not bring atonement, yet it needs the top of the יסוד. Surely the first sprinkling of an עולה, which does bring atonement, needs it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: Why do I need a verse for the top of the base? It is a קל וחומר: the leftover blood of a sin offering does not bring atonement, and still it must go on the top of the base. The first sprinkling of a burnt offering does bring atonement, so isn't it logical that it must go on the top of the base?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל questions whether the verse is needed at all, since simple logic could teach the same rule. רבי עקיבא makes a similar argument in the next step, and step 7 explains what the פסוק teaches instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר compares a weaker case with a stronger one. Leftover חטאת blood (שירים) does not bring כפרה, yet it needs גג יסוד. The main sprinkling of an עולה does bring כפרה, so it should need גג יסוד even more, which would make the פסוק unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one
The leftover blood of a sin offering, poured out after the sprinklings
Brings atonement
The first, main sprinkling of a burnt offering's blood
"Is it not logical?", the closing words of a קל וחומר
"Why do I need a verse?"

steps.whyThisMatters: This step tests whether the verse's teaching could come from logic alone. That pushes the sugya to explain why the פסוק is still needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
Why do I need a verse for the top of the base?
It is an a fortiori argument:
Just as the leftover blood of a sin offering, which does not bring atonement,
requires the top of the base;
the first sprinkling of a burnt offering, which does bring atonement,
is it not logical that it requires the top of the base?!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּג יְסוֹד לְמָה לִי קְרָא? קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the verse is needed for the rule set out in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a פסוק to teach גג יסוד for the עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from שירי חטאת, which do not bring atonement yet need גג יסוד, already teaches that the main sprinkling of an עולה, which does bring atonement, needs it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's version of the logical argument
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא makes the same kind of קל וחומר as רבי ישמעאל, adding that leftover חטאת blood does not even come to atone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: The leftover blood of a חטאת does not atone and does not come to atone, yet it needs the top of the יסוד. The first sprinkling of an עולה does atone and does come to atone. Isn't it logical that it needs the top of the יסוד too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא joins רבי ישמעאל's challenge. He argues by logic that a פסוק should not be needed to teach that an עולה's blood goes on the top of the יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument matches רבי ישמעאל's, with one addition: leftover blood 'does not come to atone.' If even this weaker blood needs the top of the יסוד, the stronger blood of an עולה surely does. The small wording difference between the two תנאים is discussed in steps 8–10.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood of a sin offering, poured out after the main sprinklings
Does not come to bring atonement
The first (main) sprinkling of a burnt offering's blood
Is it not logical? This is the opening of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
Just as the leftover blood of a sin offering,
which does not atone and does not come to atone,
requires the top of the base;
then the first sprinkling of a burnt offering,
which atones and comes to atone,
is it not logical that it requires the top of the base?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רבי ישמעאל's challenge in step 5, with added wording
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that the word 'altar' teaches גג יסוד for an עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if weaker leftover blood needs גג יסוד, the stronger first sprinkling of an עולה surely does, so no פסוק is needed

steps.title: The verse teaches that the altar of an עולה must have a base
steps.stepSummary: Since logic already teaches גג יסוד, the verse is used for a different lesson: the altar of the עולה must have a יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'at the base of the altar of the burnt offering'? To teach: give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes by giving the verse a new job. Since the top-of-the-יסוד rule comes from logic, the verse teaches that the altar used for an עולה must have a יסוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the קל וחומר makes the earlier reading unnecessary, the extra words must teach something else. The new lesson is about the altar itself: the outer altar, where the עולה is brought, needs a יסוד, so leftover blood sprinkled on it is poured on that יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
Give (provide) a base
The altar of the burnt offering, which is the outer altar

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase 'base of the altar of the burnt offering' ends up teaching that the altar of the עולה must have a יסוד. The top-of-the-יסוד rule comes from a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say
"at the base of the altar of the burnt offering"?
Give a base to the altar of the burnt offering.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'its altar,' is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenges of steps 5 and 6 by giving the verse a new meaning
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse teaches that an עולה's blood goes on the top of the יסוד
steps.terutzMaskana: That comes from logic. The verse teaches that the altar of the עולה must have a יסוד

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי ישמעאל's and רבי עקיבא's arguments.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא worded their arguments differently. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reached the same conclusion, but רבי עקיבא added 'and does not come to atone.' The גמרא wants to know what halachic difference that extra phrase reflects.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: The question compares רבי ישמעאל (step 5) and רבי עקיבא (step 6).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an inquiry into the wording difference between steps 5 and 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי ישמעאל's and רבי עקיבא's formulations

steps.title: רב אדא: whether leftover blood is essential
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says they argue whether failing to pour the leftover blood disqualifies the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: The difference is whether the leftover blood is essential. One holds it is essential, and one holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the question. The two תנאים argue about whether pouring the leftover blood is required for the offering to be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said the leftovers 'do not come to atone,' so for him they are not essential. רבי ישמעאל left that phrase out, so for him the leftovers are essential, and skipping them disqualifies the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood
Essential. Without it, the offering is invalid
One master holds

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Whether the leftover blood is essential is the difference between them:
one master holds it is essential,
and one master holds it is not essential.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether leftover blood is essential: רבי ישמעאל says yes, רבי עקיבא says no

steps.title: רב פפא: squeezing the blood of a bird חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says all agree leftover blood is not essential. The argument is about whether squeezing out a bird חטאת's blood is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees leftover blood is not essential. Here they argue whether squeezing out the blood of a bird sin offering is essential. One holds it is essential, and one holds it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer to the same question. He moves the argument away from leftover blood and onto the squeezing of a bird חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב פפא, both תנאים agree that leftover blood does not hold back the offering. Their wording difference reflects a different case: the מיצוי, squeezing the bird's blood onto the altar. רבי ישמעאל holds that it is essential, and רבי עקיבא holds that it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Squeezing out the remaining blood
A bird sin offering
They disagree

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not adding to רב אדא. He disagrees with him. For רב פפא, nobody holds that leftover blood is essential.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees that the leftover blood is not essential;
and here, about squeezing the blood of a bird sin offering,
whether it is essential, they disagree:
one master holds it is essential,
and one master holds it is not essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא – שִׁירַיִם אֵין מְעַכְּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to step 8, disagreeing with step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All agree leftovers are not essential. They argue whether squeezing a bird חטאת's blood is essential

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רב פפא begins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supporting רב פפא begins. The extra word 'the bull' teaches that the bull of יום הכיפורים needs blood placed on the יסוד, according to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב פפא: 'And all the blood he shall pour out.' Why does the verse say 'of the bull'? To teach about the bull of יום הכיפורים, that its blood must be placed on the יסוד. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to bring a ברייתא that supports רב פפא's view. This part only gives רבי's lesson from the word 'the bull.' The actual support comes in steps 14–17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is about a bull, so the word 'the bull' seems extra. רבי uses it to teach that another bull, the פר יום הכיפורים, also needs its leftover blood placed on the יסוד. This sets up the proof that leftover blood is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports him
The bull brought by the כהן גדול on יום הכיפורים
Placing blood on the base of the altar

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with Rav Pappa:
"And all the blood he shall pour out"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:7. The full verse says 'all the blood of the bull,' and that is the word being asked about.

phrases.english: Why does the verse say "the bull"?
It teaches about the bull of Yom Kippur,
that it requires placing blood on the base.
These are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב פפא's view in step 10
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that even רבי ישמעאל agrees leftover blood is not essential
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding the extra word 'הפר' in ויקרא 4:7 as teaching about פר יום הכיפורים

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר for the יסוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues that the bull of יום הכיפורים needs יסוד through a קל וחומר from the פר כהן משיח, whose blood is not brought inside as a fixed obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: This is a קל וחומר. The כהן גדול's sin-offering bull is not an obligatory offering whose blood must be brought inside, and it still needs יסוד. The יום הכיפורים bull's blood must be brought inside every year. Isn't it logical that it needs יסוד?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל says we don't need a verse to teach that the יום הכיפורים bull needs יסוד. Simple logic already proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaker case is the פר כהן משיח: it is only brought if the כהן גדול sins, so it is not a fixed duty, yet it needs יסוד. The stronger case is the יום הכיפורים bull, which is an obligation every year. If the weaker one needs יסוד, the stronger one surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
Inside the Sanctuary (the היכל)
A fixed obligation (here, an offering that must be brought regardless)
Requires pouring the blood on the base of the outer altar
Isn't it only logical?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said: It is a kal vachomer;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִם מִי שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָס דָּמוֹ לִפְנִים חוֹבָה –
phrases.english: and if one whose blood does not go inside as an obligation
phrases.notes: This is the כהן גדול's sin-offering bull. Its blood does go inside, but it's only brought if he sins, so it's not a fixed duty.

phrases.english: requires the base,
then one whose blood goes inside as an obligation
phrases.notes: The bull of יום הכיפורים, brought every single year.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it requires the base?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical source in place of רבי's verse-based source for the same law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכיפורים bull needs יסוד, proven by a קל וחומר from the פר כהן משיח.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's different קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא builds the קל וחומר based on entering the קודש הקדשים: the פר כהן משיח never goes there, yet needs יסוד, so the יום הכיפורים bull surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: The כהן גדול's bull, whose blood never enters the קודש הקדשים, not as an obligation and not as a מצוה, still needs יסוד. The יום הכיפורים bull, whose blood must enter the קודש הקדשים, surely needs יסוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא reaches the same conclusion as רבי ישמעאל, but he builds the logic differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל compared the two bulls by whether bringing their blood inside is a fixed obligation. רבי עקיבא compares them by how far the blood goes: the פר כהן משיח only reaches the היכל and never the קודש הקדשים, while the יום הכיפורים bull's blood must go all the way in. Either way, the weaker bull needs יסוד, so the stronger one surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost chamber, the קודש הקדשים
A commanded act, even if not a strict requirement
The sin-offering bull of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמוֹ נִכְנַס לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים,
phrases.english: And if one whose blood does not enter the innermost sanctum,
whether as an obligation or as a מצוה,
requires the base,

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁנִּכְנַס דָּמוֹ חוֹבָה לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים –
phrases.english: then one whose blood enters the innermost sanctum as an obligation
is it not logical that it requires the base?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וּמָה מִי שֶׁאֵין דָּמוֹ נִכְנַס לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel קל וחומר reaching the same law with a different point of comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכיפורים bull needs יסוד, because even the פר כהן משיח, which never enters the קודש הקדשים, needs it.

steps.title: The יסוד does not hold back the offering
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think missing the יסוד disqualifies the יום הכיפורים bull. The verse 'and when he has finished atoning' shows the atonement is already complete. This is רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think leaving out the יסוד ruins the offering. The verse says, 'And when he has finished atoning for the Sanctuary.' This shows all the atonements are already complete. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the יסוד step is essential, and answers no, using a verse. It labels this as רבי ישמעאל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the blood has been sprinkled inside, the Torah calls the atonement 'finished,' even before the יסוד. So the יסוד is a required step, but skipping it does not disqualify the offering. This connects to the earlier question of what exactly is essential (steps 9–10).

keyTerms.meaning: It holds it back, meaning it is essential and disqualifies the offering if missed
The verse teaches
'And when he has finished atoning'
Acts of atonement

steps.confusionAlert: 'Requires יסוד' and 'יסוד is essential' are two different things. Here the יסוד is still required, but missing it does not ruin the offering.

phrases.english: Might it be essential?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether skipping the יסוד would disqualify the bull.

phrases.english: The verse states: "And when he has finished atoning for the Sanctuary"
all the atonements are completed.
This is the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the יסוד is required, the ברייתא clarifies that it is not essential.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יסוד of the יום הכיפורים bull does not disqualify the offering if missed, because the atonement is complete after the inner sprinklings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of the support for רב פפא: רבי ישמעאל himself says that skipping the יסוד does not disqualify the offering. That contradicts רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that for רבי ישמעאל the שירים are essential.

steps.title: Proving the פר כהן משיח needs יסוד
steps.stepSummary: By the same reasoning, a קל וחומר from the שעיר נשיא, whose blood never goes inside yet needs יסוד, would teach that the פר כהן משיח, whose blood does go inside, needs יסוד. That makes the פסוק about the פר כהן משיח look unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: From now on, we can make a קל וחומר for the כהן גדול's bull from the king's goat. The king's goat never has its blood brought inside, not as an obligation and not as a מצוה, yet it needs יסוד. The כהן גדול's bull has its blood brought inside. Isn't it logical that it needs יסוד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that by the same logic, the יסוד of the פר כהן משיח could also be learned from a קל וחומר from the שעיר נשיא. That makes its explicit פסוק look unnecessary, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר נשיא is an ordinary outer sin-offering. Its blood stays outside, and the Torah says it needs יסוד. The פר כהן משיח is more serious, since its blood goes into the היכל, so logic alone would teach that it needs יסוד. Then why does the Torah write it explicitly in ויקרא 4:7? The next step raises that question.

keyTerms.meaning: The sin-offering goat of the king
From now on, based on this

steps.whatToRemember: Because a קל וחומר from the שעיר נשיא already teaches that the פר כהן משיח needs יסוד, its explicit פסוק must be there for some other reason. The next steps explain that reason.

phrases.aramaic: קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְפַר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ מִשְּׂעִיר נָשִׂיא, מֵעַתָּה:
phrases.english: From now: a kal vachomer for the bull of the anointed priest from the goat of the king:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מִי שֶׁאֵין נִכְנָס דָּמוֹ לִפְנִים,
phrases.english: And if one whose blood does not go inside,
neither as an obligation nor as a מצוה,
requires the base,
then one whose blood goes inside
whether as an obligation or as a מצוה,
is it not logical that it requires the base?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר לְפַר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ מִשְּׂעִיר נָשִׂיא, מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same kind of logic to show that the explicit verse for the פר כהן משיח's יסוד seems unneeded, setting up step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Logic from the שעיר נשיא would already teach that the פר כהן משיח needs יסוד, so its explicit verse must teach something more.

steps.title: Could skipping the leftover blood disqualify the offering?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether failing to pour the leftover blood of the פר כהן משיח on the יסוד disqualifies it. It brings the פסוק 'ואת כל דם הפר ישפך' to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think skipping it disqualifies the offering. So the פסוק says: 'And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe pouring the leftover blood is so important that skipping it ruins the offering. It quotes a פסוק to answer, and the next step explains how the פסוק works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since step 15 showed that logic alone teaches the פר כהן משיח needs יסוד, one might think the Torah wrote the פסוק to make the יסוד essential. The ברייתא rejects this from the special wording of ויקרא 4:7, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think' — introduces a mistaken idea the ברייתא will reject
Holds back / makes essential, so the offering is invalid without it
'The verse teaches' — brings the פסוק that settles the question
He shall pour out (the leftover blood at the יסוד)

phrases.english: One might think it disqualifies it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means skipping the pouring of the leftover blood on the יסוד.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:7. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, matching the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא. Now that the יסוד is shown to be required, it asks whether it is also essential.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא raises the question of disqualification and brings ויקרא 4:7 to answer it.

steps.title: Leftover blood does not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק's wording sets the pouring apart as a separate command, making it 'leftovers of the מצוה.' So leftovers do not disqualify, which supports רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק separated it into its own positive command and made it the leftovers of the מצוה. This teaches you that leftovers do not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the פסוק shows that pouring the leftover blood is not essential. This ends the proof for רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'all the blood' first, which sets this action apart from the essential sprinklings. That makes it a שירי מצוה, a 'leftover' part of the מצוה that is required but not essential. So even רבי ישמעאל, who requires the יסוד, agrees that skipping it does not invalidate the offering, just as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse detached it, setting it apart from the other steps
A positive command
The 'leftovers' of a מצוה: required, but not essential
Leftover blood does not disqualify the offering

steps.whatToRemember: Pouring the leftover blood on the יסוד is a מצוה, but skipping it does not disqualify the offering: שירים אין מעכבין.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Required' and 'essential' are different things. The יסוד is required (Steps 12–15), but it is not essential (this step).

phrases.english: The verse detached it into a separate positive command,
and made it the leftovers of the מצוה;
to tell you:
the leftovers do not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְּקוֹ הַכָּתוּב לַעֲשֵׂה, וַעֲשָׂאוֹ שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in Step 16 answers the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שירים אין מעכבין. The ברייתא backs רב פפא: רבי ישמעאל agrees that skipping the יסוד does not disqualify the offering.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's view that רבי ישמעאל does not consider the leftover blood essential

steps.title: Does רבי ישמעאל really hold squeezing a bird's blood is essential?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי ישמעאל holds מיצוי חטאת העוף is essential. It quotes a teaching from his school on 'והנשאר בדם ימצה' that seems to say otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי ישמעאל really hold that squeezing out the blood of a bird sin offering is essential? But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And the remainder of the blood shall be squeezed out' means it is squeezed out only if some remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks another part of רב פפא's explanation: the idea that, for רבי ישמעאל, squeezing out a bird's blood is essential. It quotes his school's teaching, and the rest of that teaching continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ישמעאל's school reads the פסוק to mean 'squeeze it out only if blood remains,' then squeezing cannot be essential. That contradicts the claim that רבי ישמעאל holds מיצוי מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing out the bird's blood against the wall of the מזבח
A bird sin offering
'But it was taught' — brings a source to challenge a claim
The study house (school) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: And does רבי ישמעאל hold
that squeezing out the blood of a bird sin offering is essential?!
phrases.notes: This is how רב פפא explained רבי ישמעאל's view back in step 10.
